pr_title: fix(‎LibCarla): port lane marking, waypoint  loop, lane corners, and pugixml null fixes

goldens.comment: In Map.cpp, the new `continue` on degenerate `edges` skips the `s_current += distancebetweentrees` step at the end of the loop. If `edges.first == edges.second` persists, the loop no longer makes progress and can hang.
goldens.expected_evidence: Point to Map.cpp's while loop where `if (edges.first == edges.second) continue;` bypasses the bottom-of-loop `s_current += distancebetweentrees;` increment.
goldens.raw_comment: Confirmed bug. The `s_current += distancebetweentrees;` increment lives at the bottom of the `while` body, so the new `continue` skips it and any persistently degenerate `edges.first == edges.second` will hang the function. This needs to be fixed before merge.

goldens.comment: In MeshFactory.cpp, the refactor changes lane-mark edge computation to always use the extra lane width, which alters the previous solid/final-segment behavior that used zero extra width. This shifts lane marking positions on roads with non-zero extra lane width.
goldens.expected_evidence: Point to MeshFactory.cpp call sites where ComputeEdgesForLanemark replaced direct GetCornerPositions(..., 0) behavior and now always uses extra lane width.
goldens.raw_comment:
Good catch. Confirmed: the old `Solid` case and the final-segment call passed `extra_width = 0`, while the `Broken` cases used `road_param.extra_lane_width`. The refactor unifies them on `road_param.extra_lane_width`, which silently shifts solid lane marking positions on maps with non-zero extra lane width. To preserve the original behavior exactly, please add an `extra_width` parameter to `ComputeEdgesForLanemark` and forward `0` from the call sites that previously used it.

Probably the best action right now is to create a new issue ticket and track this possible issue separately.

goldens.comment: The OpenSSL-1.0.2+ fallback branch in src/event/ngx_event_openssl.c calls SSL_get_sigalgs() behind a version check that does not exclude AWS-LC, so this code can fail to compile when that function is unavailable.
goldens.expected_evidence: Point to the #elif branch in src/event/ngx_event_openssl.c that calls SSL_get_sigalgs() under an OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER check that can still include AWS-LC, where the API is absent.
goldens.raw_comment:
This won't build on AWS-LC, so needs to be guarded.

src/event/ngx_event_openssl.c:5733:9: error: call to undeclared function 'SSL_get_sigalgs'; ISO C99 and later do not support implicit function declarations [-Werror,-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

Given that, I tend to think that we really need to use the `SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS` guard instead,
as a good indicator of the SSL_get_sigalgs() presence, both added in OpenSSL 1.0.2.
The macro is only defined in the versions that provide SSL_get_sigalgs() API and unlikely to be changed:

```
$ grep -rw SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS boringssl/include libressl-*/include openssl-*/include openssl-*/ssl/ssl.h | grep define

openssl-1.1.1/include/openssl/ssl.h:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97
openssl-3.0/include/openssl/ssl.h:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97
openssl-3.0/include/openssl/ssl.h.in:#define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS 97
openssl-3.1/include/openssl/ssl.h:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97

openssl-3.3/include/openssl/ssl.h.in:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97
openssl-3.4/include/openssl/ssl.h:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97
openssl-3.4/include/openssl/ssl.h.in:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97
openssl-3.5/include/openssl/ssl.h:#define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS 97
openssl-3.5/include/openssl/ssl.h.in:#define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS 97
openssl-3.6/include/openssl/ssl.h.in:#define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS 97
openssl-4.0/include/openssl/ssl.h:#define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS 97
openssl-4.0/include/openssl/ssl.h.in:#define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS 97
openssl-1.0.2/ssl/ssl.h:# define SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS                    97
```

```
$ grep -rw SSL_get_sigalgs boringssl/include libressl-*/include openssl-*/include openssl-*/ssl/tls1.h 
openssl-1.1.0/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-1.1.1/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.0/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.1/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.2/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.3/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.4/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.5/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-3.6/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-4.0/include/openssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
openssl-1.0.2/ssl/tls1.h:int SSL_get_sigalgs(SSL *s, int idx,
```

SSL_get_sigalgs() was added in e7f8ff4382:
date:       Tue Mar 6 14:28:21 2012 +0000
description:
New ctrls to retrieve supported signature algorithms and curves and
extensions to s_client and s_server to print out retrieved valued.

SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS was added in 0f229cce65:
date:       Fri Jun 22 14:03:31 2012 +0000
description:
Add support for application defined signature algorithms for use with
TLS v1.2. These are sent as an extension for clients and during a certificate
request for servers.

Both were removed in 2015 in BoringSSL in 3dd9016a5 (and thus in AWS-LC).
And LibreSSL was forked off OpenSSL 1.0.1-something, so it predates these two changes.

goldens.comment: In src/cluster.c:isValidAuxChar, `isalnum` is still called with `c` instead of the unsigned-cast `ch`. Passing a negative non-EOF value to `isalnum` is undefined behavior on platforms with signed `char`.
goldens.expected_evidence: Point to src/cluster.c:isValidAuxChar using isalnum(c) after casting to unsigned char ch, which leaves ctype called on possibly negative values.
goldens.raw_comment:
On platforms where char is signed (e.g. ARM by default), high-bit bytes (0x80–0xFF) sign-extend to negative int. isalnum(negative) is undefined behavior per C11 §7.4¶1; in practice glibc range-checks but musl/macOS may not. The
PR already declared ch for exactly this reason — finish the job. CodeRabbit raised the same point.

```suggestion
    if (isalnum(ch)) return 1;
```

goldens.comment: In `isValidAuxChar` (cluster.c), `strchr(invalid_charset, c)` passes the original signed `int c` instead of the already-declared `unsigned char ch`; high-bit byte values sign-extend to negative integers, producing undefined behavior per C11 §7.4¶1.
goldens.expected_evidence: In isValidAuxChar, `strchr(invalid_charset, c)` uses the original signed int `c` instead of `unsigned char ch`, same UB as the isalnum call above.
